title: Regulatory fragmentation for gene-edited crops
bottleneck: Gene-edited crops face wildly inconsistent regulation: EU courts subjected CRISPR plants to full GMO approval costing about $35M per trait, the US SECURE rule seesawed in federal court, and many developing countries lack frameworks entirely — while the science shows edits equivalent to conventional breeding. Developers must navigate contradictory regimes, and only the largest companies can afford multi-jurisdiction approval.
why_it_blocks: Regulatory chaos delays or kills climate-resilient varieties. Beneficial traits sit in labs while farmers face the stresses they were bred to resist.
current_state: The EU is legislating new genomic technique categories with contested edit limits; the US product-based approach faces legal challenges; global harmonization is distant.
